record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let p be a polynomial in C[x1, ..., xn] such that the hypersurface X = {p = 0} is contractible and has an isolated singular point. Must p be equivalent, up to an automorphism of C^3, to a quasihomogeneous polynomial?

evidence.quote:
2.3. QUASIHOMOGENEITY CONJECTURE. If X as above has an isolated
singular point, then the polynomial p is equivalent, up to an automorphism of C3
, to a
quasihomogeneous one.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let p ∈ ℂ[x₁, x₂, x₃] be a polynomial such that the affine algebraic hypersurface X = {p = 0} ⊂ ℂ³ is contractible (as a topological space) and has exactly one singular point, which is isolated. A polynomial q ∈ ℂ[x₁, x₂, x₃] is called quasihomogeneous if there exist positive integers w₁, w₂, w₃ and d such that q(t^{w₁}x₁, t^{w₂}x₂, t^{w₃}x₃) = t^d q(x₁, x₂, x₃) for all t ∈ ℂ. Two polynomials p, q are said to be equivalent up to an automorphism of ℂ³ if there exists a polynomial automorphism Φ: ℂ³ → ℂ³ such that q = p ∘ Φ.

Question: Must every such p be equivalent, up to an automorphism of ℂ³, to a quasihomogeneous polynomial?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive resolution of this quasihomogeneity conjecture for contractible hypersurfaces in ℂ³ with an isolated singularity. Related work on quasihomogeneous isolated hypersurface singularities (Saito-type criteria, classification of weight systems, Yau–Zuo characterizations) exists, but none of the retrieved sources explicitly settle the conjecture as stated. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Complex hypersurfaces diffeomorphic to affine spaces (Choudary–Dimca)
status_evidence.snippet: Studies complex hypersurfaces in C^n that are diffeomorphic/contractible to affine spaces, closely related to the conjecture but not resolving the C^3 quasihomogeneity statement.
status_evidence.claim: Related context but no resolution of the conjecture is asserted.

status_evidence.title: Nine characterizations of quasihomogeneity (survey)
status_evidence.snippet: Reviews characterizations of quasihomogeneous isolated hypersurface singularities (e.g. Saito's theorem) but does not address the global contractibility-based conjecture for C^3.
